candidate.title: scRC-Seq
candidate.scope: The five-operation scRC-Seq row of the supplied Illumina poster, interpreted at schematic level using the cited Upton et al. (2015) single-nucleus L1 capture implementation: starting suspension, FACS isolation, nucleus picking, whole-genome amplification, sequencing-library construction and sequence capture to an enriched DNA library. The left-hand Novel retrotransposition events and Retrotransposon binding site/Genomic DNA cartoons explain the target; no arrow transfers them into a separate branch. MALBAC is an embedded amplification component. The adjacent scAba-seq and scATAC-Seq rows and the right-hand chemistry panel are outside this target. The row ends at enriched library; downstream sequencing is described only to interpret that product.

operations.label: Sequence capture
operations.description: Enrich the sequencing library for fragments containing the targeted retrotransposon sequence and its contiguous genomic flank. The drawing shows the target-marked fragment contacting a short capture element above a gray semicircular symbol, followed by an arrow to the Enriched library product.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper resolves the capture chemistry as hybridization to LNA probes targeting the extreme 5′ and 3′ ends of L1-Ta. The probes are 5ʹ-biotinylated for streptavidin-bead capture. The paper processes the two L1 ends in separate capture reactions; the poster represents them within one broad Sequence capture block, without depicting the internal split or recombination.
operations.information_effect: The enriched DNA carries L1-genome junctions. Downstream paired-end sequencing can span a junction and locate an insertion using the genomic flank; sequencing is not itself drawn in this row. Capture also recovers reference and polymorphic L1 copies, so enrichment alone does not establish a novel or somatic event. Somatic assignment in the paper uses comparisons and filtering, with chimera/duplicate handling. One or both L1 junctions may be recovered: 3′ capture detects typical insertions, whereas 5′ capture favors full-length or heavily 5′-truncated insertions. Incomplete detection and WGA dropout mean that absence from the library does not establish absence from the original genome.

method_scopes.rationale: scRC-Seq is the only target named by the card and assigned row; Single-cell RC-seq and single-cell retrotransposon capture sequencing are naming variants of that target. All five local operations belong to its arrow-connected route. The matching collection heading and the Upton full text identify a single-nucleus L1 implementation within the broader retrotransposon capture assay family; this does not assert identical preparation for every family member. MALBAC is an internal WGA component. The paper’s WGS quality-control route, bulk comparisons, and separate end-specific capture reactions clarify the implementation/readout but are not drawn branches or alternative targets in this poster row. The secondary page’s inline reference 147 points to a modified-cytosine mapping title rather than the matching Upton citation numbered 148. That catalogue citation is assessed only at its supplied bibliographic level and is not adopted as a method paper or architecture support.
